To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: IMPORTANT: Brightline Pro 6% developer, batch LX2291 is 12%

Hi all,

Please read this before you mix anything today, especially if you've bought developer off the Kelvin Trade rep in the last few weeks.

**What's wrong**

Kelvin Trade have sent out a notice saying one batch of **Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer 1L** might have **12% (40 vol)** in it. It's labelled 6% but it's not.

- Batch: **LX2291**
- Supplied between 19 October and 5 November 2026
- Other batches and other strengths aren't affected (according to them)

Their email said "sorry for any inconvenience." It's a lot more than an inconvenience, so please take it seriously.

**How to check your bottles**

- The batch number is **on the base of the bottle only**. It's not on the box. Don't check the box and assume you're fine. Tip every bottle up and look at the bottom.
- Check the **open bottles in your trolley** as well as the stock in the back.
- If it says LX2291, stop using it and put it aside with a note on it so nobody grabs it by mistake.

A few of us bought off the same rep, so even if you think you didn't get any, please check anyway.

**What it does**

Two of us have had problems with it in the last week:

- **Very fast lift.** One bleach retouch was at pale yellow in under 20 minutes when it normally takes 35 to 40.
- **Foils getting really hot.** Aileen thought it was the heater being too close, so don't write it off as that.
- **Brassy, patchy results** on highlights.
- **Scalp burn.** A client went from the usual tingle to burning at the crown at around 18 minutes. She was left with a red patch at the crown and a few spots at the nape.

If a client's colour or lightener is doing anything odd since you got new developer, check the bottle.

**If someone reacts in the chair**

- Stop and get the product off. Rinse with **cool running water** for at least 20 minutes, and keep going if it's still stinging. No shampoo.
- Take the gown off them if any product has got on it. Keep your gloves on.
- Don't put creams or anything else on it.
- Burns from chemicals should be looked at. Tell them to phone **NHS 24 on 111** or go to a minor injuries unit, and write it down for them.
- **Phone 999** straight away if they're having trouble breathing, their face or throat is swelling, they feel faint or collapse, or the burn is big or deep.
- Write it up in the **incident book** at the desk.

**If you've had a problem with it**

- **Keep at least one bottle. Don't bin it.** If anything comes of it, you'll need it.
- Take dated photos of the bottle base showing the batch number, and of any reaction (if the client is OK with that).
- Write down what you mixed, the ratio, the timings and what happened while it's fresh in your mind.
- Keep the Kelvin Trade email.
- If you have public liability insurance, phone them early.

**Returning it**

You get full credit back. The rep is in on **Tuesday**, so you can give the bottles to him then. Or you can take them to the **Hillington depot** yourself. Remember to keep one back if you've had a problem.

If you're not sure about a bottle, give me a shout and I'll look at it with you. Better to check twice than end up with what we had this week.

Kirsty

reasons: The first-aid advice contradicts the supplied guidance to call 999 immediately and rinse for about an hour, and the notice incorrectly states the batch is definitely 12%.
